items.statement: F/F^+ is a CM extension, G/F^+ a unitary group with G ×_{F^+} F ≅ GL_n and G(F^+ ⊗_Q R) compact, every place of F^+ above p split in F, ℘ a fixed place above p with K := F^+_℘ ≅ F_{℘̃}; for v ∈ S_p∖{℘} a dominant weight ξ_v and an inertial type τ_v give σ(τ_v) ⊗_E L(ξ_v) and a lattice W_{ξ,τ}. For a sufficiently small tame level U^℘ one forms S_{ξ,τ}(U^℘U_℘, O_E/ϖ^k) of functions on G(F^+)∖G(A^∞_{F^+}) transforming under U^℘U_℘, and Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E) := (lim_k lim_{U_℘} S_{ξ,τ})⊗_{O_E}E, an admissible unitary Banach representation of GL_n(K).
items.note: AF.5 identifies algebraic modular forms on groups compact at infinity with functions on finite adelic double cosets valued in an algebraic representation; the completed version Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E) is the p-adic limit of exactly those spaces. Source issue: W_{ξ,τ} is printed as a lattice in a single σ(τ_v) ⊗ L(ξ_v) although it is acted on by ∏_{v∈S_p∖{℘}} U_v and must be a lattice in the tensor product over those v.

items.name: The Hecke algebra T(U^℘) and the maximal ideal m_ρ attached to ρ
items.statement: T(U^℘) is the polynomial O_E-algebra on the operators T^{(j)}_{ṽ} = [U_v ι_ṽ^{-1} diag(1_{n-j}, ϖ_ṽ 1_j) U_v] for v ∉ S split in F and j = 1,…,n, acting on Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E) commuting with GL_n(K). To a continuous ρ: Gal_{F,S} → GL_n(E) with ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗_E ε^{1-n} is attached the maximal ideal m_ρ generated by the (-1)^j(#k_ṽ)^{j(j-1)/2}T^{(j)}_{ṽ} - a^{(j)}_{ṽ}, where the a^{(j)}_{ṽ} are the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of ρ(Frob_ṽ).
items.note: SR.1 builds the Hecke algebras and their double-coset operators; AF.5 the dictionary with automorphic forms. The normalisation with the signs and the powers of #k_ṽ is the one that makes m_ρ match the Galois side.

items.name: The eigenvariety E(U^℘), its sheaf M(U^℘), and classical and generic points
items.statement: Emerton's construction applied to J_B(Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)^{Q_p-an}) gives a rigid space E(U^℘) with a map κ to T̂ and a coherent sheaf M(U^℘) with M(U^℘)^∨ = J_B(Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)^{Q_p-an})^∨; a point is a pair (δ,ω) with ω: T(U^℘) ↠ E, and lies on E(U^℘) iff Hom_{T(K)}(δ, J_B(Ŝ^{Q_p-an}[m_ω])) ≠ 0. It is classical when the same holds with Ŝ^lalg, and such a point has δ = δ_smδ_alg; it is generic when δ_smδ_B^{-1}|·|_K∘θ is a generic character.
items.note: Eigenvarieties for definite unitary groups are not planned anywhere in the atlas; O0 builds weight spaces and locally analytic representations for overconvergent forms, and PadicFamilies L2 the eigenvariety machine in the Hilbert/elliptic setting. The construction here is Emerton's, from the Jacquet module of a completed Banach space.

items.name: Proposition 4.14: basic geometry of E(U^℘)
items.statement: (1) E(U^℘) is equidimensional of dimension nd_K; (2) M(U^℘) is Cohen–Macaulay over E(U^℘); (3) E(U^℘) is reduced.
items.note: Deduced from Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)|_H ≅ C(H,E)^{⊕s} for a compact open H (Breuil–Ding Lem. 6.1) and the Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen machinery; reducedness follows Chenevier's argument.

items.name: Hypothesis 4.15: vanishing of the adjoint Selmer group
items.statement: The composition Ext^1_{g,S_p∖{℘}}(ρ,ρ) → Ext^1(D,D) → Ext^1(D,D)/Ext^1_g(D,D) is injective, where Ext^1_U(ρ,ρ) is the space of deformations ρ̃ with ρ̃^c ≅ ρ̃^∨ ⊗_E ε^{1-n} and Ext^1_{g,S_p∖{℘}}(ρ,ρ) is the subspace that is de Rham at every place of S_p other than ℘. In particular Ext^1_U(D,D) ∩ Ext^1_g(D,D) = 0.
items.note: Known in many cases: Allen Thm. A, Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen Cor. 4.12, Newton–Thorne Thm. A. It is the only global input besides classicality.

items.name: The Galois family on the eigenvariety and its properties
items.statement: On a small enough affinoid X ⊂ E(U^℘) around z_w there is a pseudo-character T_X: Gal_{F,S} → O(X) interpolating the ρ_z (Chenevier), which for ρ absolutely irreducible comes from a representation ρ_X: Gal_{F,S} → GL_n(O(X)) (Bergdall) such that (i) ρ_X^c ≅ ρ_X^∨ ⊗_E ε^{1-n}, (ii) ρ_{X,ṽ} is de Rham of weights ξ_v - θ^{F^+_v} for v ∈ S_p∖{℘}, and (iii) D_rig(ρ_{X,℘̃}) over R_{K,X} is a successive extension of the R_{K,X}(δ_{X,i}|·|_K^{2i-(n+1)}ε^{1-i}).
items.note: (ii) uses Berger–Colmez; (iii) is the global triangulation theorem of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao/Liu in Bergdall's paraboline form, applicable because D is non-critical and φ-generic. Source issue: (i) is printed ρ_X^c ≅ ρ_X ⊗_E ε^{1-n}, without the dual, twice.

items.name: Proposition 4.17: smoothness of E(U^℘) at the companion points and Hypothesis 4.10
items.statement: Assume Hypothesis 4.15 and ρ absolutely irreducible. Then E(U^℘) is smooth at z_w for every w ∈ S_n, and Ext^1_U(D,D) — the image of Ext^1_{g,S_p∖{℘}}(ρ,ρ) in Ext^1(D,D) — satisfies Hypothesis 4.10 (1) and (2).
items.note: The tangent space T_{z_w} injects into Ext^1_U(ρ,ρ) with image in Ext^1_{g,S_p∖{℘}}(ρ,ρ) and then into Ext^1_{U,w}(D,D), so dim T_{z_w} ≤ nd_K = dim E(U^℘), which forces equality and smoothness.

items.name: Theorem 4.18: local–global compatibility for the definite unitary group
items.statement: Assume Hypothesis 4.15 and ρ absolutely irreducible, with Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)^lalg[m_ρ] ≅ π_alg(φ,h)^{⊕r} and D = D_rig(ρ_{℘̃}) ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h). Let π̃ be the closed subrepresentation of Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)^{Q_p-an}_{ρ̄}[a_T] generated by the images of the ι_w. Then there is a GL_n(K) × A_{D,U}-equivariant isomorphism π̃ ≅ (π_1(φ,h)^univ_U)^{⊕r}, and consequently π_min(D)^{⊕r} ↪ Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)^{Q_p-an}[m_ρ].
items.note: This is Theorem 1.1 (2) in the non-patched setting: the same argument as in §4.1, with M(U^℘) locally free of rank r, Proposition 4.14 (2) replacing local freeness of rank one, and Corollary 4.12 replacing Theorem 3.21.

items.name: Corollaries 4.20–4.21: maximality and the determination of the Hodge parameters
items.statement: π_min(D)^{⊕r} is the maximal subrepresentation of Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)^{Q_p-an}[m_ρ] generated by extensions of π_alg(φ,h) by π_1(φ,h); and for D' ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h), π_min(D') ↪ Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)[m_ρ] if and only if D'_σ ≅ D_σ for all σ ∈ Σ_K. In particular, for K = Q_p the GL_n(Q_p)-representation Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)^{Q_p-an}[m_ρ] determines ρ_{℘̃}.
items.note: Uses that non-criticality of D is itself readable from Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)[m_ρ] by Breuil, Thm. 9.3.

items.name: The classicality input (4.14): multiplicity r of the locally algebraic vectors
items.statement: There is r ∈ Z_{≥1} with π_alg(φ,h)^{⊕r} ≅ Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)[m_ρ]^lalg, by the local–global compatibility for l = p of Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor together with Breuil–Ding (6.3).
items.note: R31.2 relates classical finite-level cohomology with algebraic coefficients to the locally algebraic vectors of completed cohomology; this is the same statement for a definite unitary group.

items.name: Global triangulation over an eigenvariety
items.statement: The theory of triangulations of families of (φ,Γ)-modules over affinoids: the relative Robba ring R_{K,X}, the fact that a family of Galois representations over a reduced affinoid with a Zariski-dense set of trianguline points is trianguline after shrinking, in the paraboline form of Bergdall and the form of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao and Liu.
items.note: PG.7 owns the affinoid/relative Robba category of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao and its source-qualified triangulation/specialisation inputs; the paper uses precisely those, applied at a smooth point of an eigenvariety.

routes.title: Locally analytic representations of p-adic reductive groups
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas builds the locally Q_p-analytic representation theory that §3.1 runs on. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups covers the smooth category only; LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0–L4 builds Q_p-analytic distributions on O_F and finite products of local integer rings and their character spaces, not the distribution algebra of a p-adic reductive group or its coadmissible modules; PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.2 constructs the locally analytic category for GL_2(Q_p) alone and in service of Colmez's functor. The Orlik–Strauch functors, the constituents and socle filtration of a locally analytic principal series of GL_n(K), Emerton's Jacquet functor with its adjunction, and Schraen's spectral sequence for Ext groups are used by this paper, by Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen and by most of the p-adic Langlands literature, so they should be planned once, for a general group, rather than inside any one application.
routes.brief: Final theorems: (i) for a p-adic reductive group G over K, construct the Schneider–Teitelbaum distribution algebra D(G,E), admissible locally Q_p-analytic representations and the anti-equivalence with coadmissible modules, and prove that Ext^1 in that category computes extensions of admissible representations; (ii) construct the Orlik–Strauch functors F^G_{P^-}(M,π) from category O for g_{Σ_K} and smooth representations of the Levi, and prove the theorem describing their irreducible constituents and when two of them agree — for GL_n and a Borel this is Proposition 3.1 of this paper, including soc PS(w(φ),h) ≅ π_alg(φ,h) and soc(PS/π_alg) ≅ ⊕_{lg(u)=1} C(w,u); (iii) construct Emerton's locally analytic Jacquet functor J_B and the closed induction I_{P^-}^G, and prove the adjunction for balanced maps (Emerton, Def. 0.8 and Thm. 0.13); (iv) prove Schraen's spectral sequence Ext^p_{T(K)}(H_q(N^-(K),V),δ) ⇒ Ext^{p+q}_G(V,(Ind_{B^-}^G δ)^an) with its separatedness hypothesis, and deduce the Ext^1 computations of §3.1: dim Ext^1(π_alg,π_alg) = n + d_K, dim Ext^1(π_alg,PS_1(w(φ),h)) = n + nd_K, dim Ext^1(π_alg,π_1(φ,h)) = n + (2^n-1)d_K, and dim Ext^1(π_alg,C(I,s_{i,σ})) = 1; (v) construct the amalgamated sums PS_1, π_1(φ,h), π(φ,h) and π_{F_P}(φ,h), prove Lemma 3.10 on which constituents survive a parabolic induction, and prove that parabolic induction is compatible with these Ext groups (Proposition 3.12); (vi) develop the locally σ-analytic and g_{Σ_K∖{σ}}-algebraic subcategories and prove the decomposition Ext^1/Ext^1_g ≅ ⊕_{τ∈Σ_K}(Ext^1_τ/Ext^1_g). Import from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1–SR.3 the smooth principal series, admissibility and the Bernstein centre; import category O, Verma modules and their composition factors from the Tau Ceti Lie highest weight roadmap rather than planning them again; import rigid character spaces from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0a. Do not plan the trianguline variety or any (φ,Γ)-module theory here: they belong to TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel.

routes.title: The trianguline variety and its local model
routes.reason: This is the roadmap proposed by PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (merged as PR #2022) for the trianguline variety, its local model and the deformation theory of trianguline (φ,Γ)-modules; nothing in the atlas plans them. §§2.1–2.4 of this paper are the infinitesimal theory of exactly those objects — trianguline and paraboline deformations of a crystabelline (φ,Γ)-module, their partially de Rham variants, and the higher intertwining relations between them — so they are sources for the same roadmap rather than a second one. Recording them here is what PROTOCOL §15 asks: the two papers feed one design job.
routes.brief: Added to the brief already proposed by PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19: plan the deformation theory of a generic non-critical crystabelline (φ,Γ)-module D over R_{K,E}. Final statements: dim Ext^1(D,D) = 1 + n²d_K, dim Ext^1_g(D,D) = 1 + (n(n-1)/2)d_K and dim Ext^1_w(D,D) = 1 + (n(n+1)/2)d_K with κ_w surjective (Proposition 2.10); the independence of Ext^1_0(D,D) = Ker κ_w of w and the Weyl-equivariance of the κ_w (Lemma 2.11); paraboline deformations with dim Ext^1_{F_P}(D,D) = 1 + d_K dim P and the isomorphism \bar{Ext}^1_{F_P}(D,D) ≅ ∏_i \bar{Ext}^1(M_i,M_i) (Proposition 2.13, Corollary 2.14); the partially de Rham theory Ext^1_σ with dim Ext^1_σ(D,D) = 1 + (n(n-1)/2)(d_K-1) + n² and its parabolic version (Lemma 2.16, Proposition 2.17); the modification D ↦ D_σ of Proposition 2.5 with 𝔗_σ: \bar{Ext}^1_*(D,D) ≅ \bar{Ext}^1_*(D_σ,D_σ) (Proposition 2.24, Corollary 2.27); the Hodge parameter ι_D ∈ Hom(D_1,C_1) with dim Hom(D_1,C_1) ≤ 2 and the theorem that ι_D determines D when K = Q_p and that ι_{D_σ} always determines D_σ (Propositions 2.2, 2.4, 2.7, 2.8 and Example 2.9 for n = 3); and the higher intertwining theorem: D̃ ∈ Ext^1_F(D,D) ∩ Ext^1_G(D,D) if and only if its graded deformation lies in Ext^1_{ι_D}(D_1,D_1) (Theorem 2.32), with the consequence that the subspace L(D,D_1,C_1) determines ι_D up to a scalar (Corollary 2.34) and its σ-analogue (Theorem 2.37, Corollary 2.38). Import the Robba ring, rank one modules and the Herr complex from PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.3/PG.7, W^+_dR, B-pairs and Fontaine's classification from PadicHodgeTheory P7, and the deformation rings from LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1/R08.3. Do not plan the GL_n(K)-side here.

routes.title: p-adic Hodge parameters in locally analytic representations of GL_n
routes.reason: The correspondence D ↦ π_min(D) is the paper's own theory and has no home in the atlas. PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp is the n = 2, K = Q_p case of the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, built through Colmez's functor, and its methods do not extend; CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility and the Part II proposed below are about where such representations occur globally, not about constructing them; the trianguline roadmap owns the Galois side. What is new here is the comparison itself: a surjection t_D from an extension group of GL_n(K)-representations that depends only on (φ,h) onto the deformation space of D, whose kernel is the Hodge parameter.
routes.brief: Final theorems, exactly as the paper states them. (1) Theorem 3.21: for D ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) the amalgamation ⊕_{w∈S_n} \bar{Ext}^1_w(D,D) ↠ \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) factors uniquely through ⊕_w Hom(T(K),E) → Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)), giving a surjection t_D with dim Ker(t_D) = (2^n - n(n+1)/2 - 1)d_K. (2) The representation π_min(D), the extension of Ker(t_D) ⊗_E π_alg(φ,h) by π_1(φ,h), characterised by Corollary 3.25: socle π_alg(φ,h), the same second socle layer as π_1(φ,h), and a bijection t_D: Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h),π_min(D)) ≅ \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) compatible with trianguline deformations refinement by refinement. (3) Its central character χ_D and infinitesimal character ξ_λ (Proposition 3.26), proved by matching the Sen-weight tangent map with the action of the centre of U(gl_{n,Σ_K}) through Harish-Chandra. (4) Compatibility with parabolic induction: ⊕_i Ker(t_{M_i}) ≅ Ker(t_D) ∩ Ext^1_{F_P}(π_alg,π_1) (Proposition 3.27), and with the embeddings σ: K ↪ E: Ker(t_D) ≅ ⊕_{σ∈Σ_K} Ker(t_{D,σ}) and π_min(D) ≅ ⊕^σ_{π_alg} π_min(D)_σ (Corollary 3.31). (5) Theorem 3.34: π_min(D)_σ ≅ π_min(D')_σ if and only if D_σ ≅ D'_σ, hence π_min(D) determines the family {D_σ}_{σ∈Σ_K}, and determines D when K = Q_p — for n ≥ 3 this is information that π_alg(φ,h), i.e. classical local Langlands together with the Hodge–Tate weights, does not contain. (6) The reformulation of §3.2.2: the Artinian algebras A_D and A_{D,w}, the universal extension π_1(φ,h)^univ, Theorem 3.36 (a unique A_D-action with π_1(φ,h)^univ_w ↪ π_1(φ,h)^univ[I_w] for every w) and Corollary 3.37 (π_min(D) ≅ π_1(φ,h)^univ[m_{A_D}]). Import the whole GL_n(K)-side from LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups and the whole Galois side from TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel; plan neither again. Record that for n = 2 the kernel is zero, so the theory is empty for GL_2, and that π_min(D) is expected to be far from the full locally analytic representation attached to D.

routes.title: Completed cohomology and p-adic local–global compatibility, Part II: eigenvarieties, classicality and companion constituents
routes.reason: §4 proves that the representation π_min(D) built locally actually occurs inside the patched Banach representation Π_∞ and inside the completed cohomology of a definite unitary group, and that it is the maximal such subrepresentation. Its parent roadmap owns completed cohomology, the patched completed module and the comparison with classical forms, but every stage of it is written for modular curves and GL_2, and none plans an eigenvariety for a definite unitary group, its tangent spaces at companion points, or the passage from a tangent computation to an embedding of locally analytic representations. This is the same Part II that PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 proposes, and §4 belongs in it rather than in a second roadmap.
routes.brief: Added to the brief already proposed by PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19. Final theorems: (1) Theorem 4.5 — with Π_∞ the patched Banach representation of Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin, ρ such that D = D_rig(ρ) ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) and Π_∞[m_x]^lalg ≠ 0, the subrepresentation of Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[a_x] generated by the images of the n! maps ι_w is isomorphic to π_1(φ,h)^univ, GL_n(K) × A_D-equivariantly; (2) Corollary 4.6 and Corollary 4.8 — π_min(D) ↪ Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[m_x], and it is the maximal subrepresentation given by extensions of π_alg(φ,h) by π_1(φ,h); with Theorem 3.34 this gives Corollary 4.9: Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[m_x] determines {D_σ}_σ, and determines ρ when K = Q_p; (3) the same statements without patching, for a definite unitary group: Hypothesis 4.15 on the adjoint Selmer group, Proposition 4.17 (smoothness of the eigenvariety E(U^℘) at the companion points z_w, and that Ext^1_U(D,D) satisfies Hypothesis 4.10), Theorem 4.18 (π_min(D)^{⊕r} ↪ Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)^{Q_p-an}[m_ρ]) and Corollaries 4.20–4.21. Plan the machinery these need: Emerton's construction of an eigenvariety from the Jacquet module of a completed Banach space, its equidimensionality of dimension nd_K, the Cohen–Macaulayness of its coherent sheaf and its reducedness (Proposition 4.14); the Galois family over an affinoid of the eigenvariety with its polarisation, partial de Rhamness and triangulation (the three properties (i)–(iii) of Proposition 4.17); and the tangent-space identification M_{x̃_w}^∨ ≅ δ̃_w^univ δ_B with the balancedness that turns it into an injection of GL_n(K)-representations. Import the patched module and the trianguline variety rather than rebuilding them, and import the whole local theory from PadicHodgeParametersInLocallyAnalyticRepresentations. Hypotheses 4.10 and 4.15 are hypotheses, not targets: record where they are known (Allen; Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen; Newton–Thorne).

routes.reason: The paper works throughout with (φ,Γ)-modules over the Robba ring rather than with Galois representations, and it uses exactly what PG.3 and PG.7 own: the Herr complex and Liu's Euler characteristic formula (every dimension count in §2.3 is an instance), rank one modules R_{K,E}(χ) and the dictionary between characters of K^× and trianguline parameters, and, over an affinoid, the relative Robba ring of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao with its global triangulation theorem, used at a smooth point of an eigenvariety in §4.2. PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 routes the same foundations to the same two layers.

P7 builds the Robba coefficient rings and the representation-theoretic handoffs of p-adic Hodge theory. The paper needs from it: W^+_dR and its decomposition over Σ_K (without which no ‘partially de Rham’ statement can even be formulated), Berger's B-pairs with the comparison of (φ,Γ)-cohomology and Galois cohomology, and Fontaine's classification of B_dR-representations, which is what produces the modified module D_σ of Proposition 2.5. The same three inputs are routed to P7 by PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19.

The smooth skeleton of the paper is standard and is already planned: normalised parabolic induction and Jacquet functors (SR.2), admissibility, irreducibility of a generic principal series and the Bernstein decomposition and centre (SR.3), and Hecke algebras with their double-coset operators (SR.1). The paper is a good source for the refinement these stages must export: the Bernstein centre's completion at π_sm(φ), the maps J_w: ∏_i Spec H_{w^{-1}(i)} → Spec H with J_{w_2} = (w_2w_1^{-1})∘J_{w_1}, and their tangent maps, which are what make the extension classes ζ_w intertwine correctly.

R08.1 owns framed local deformation rings with the tangent and obstruction description, and R08.3 the potentially semistable deformation spaces. The paper uses the (φ,Γ)-module analogues — R_D, R_{D,w}, R_{D,g} and their formal smoothness — and the trianguline variety X^□_tri(ρ̄) with its dimension and its smoothness at non-critical points. It is a good source for the tangent-space bookkeeping these layers need: the Cartesian square relating a trianguline deformation ring to the deformation ring of its parameter, and the resulting Artinian algebras A_D and A_{D,w}.

R31.5 constructs the patched completed module with its finiteness and support properties and R31.2 relates classical forms to locally algebraic vectors. §4.1 consumes precisely these: the patched Banach representation Π_∞ over R_∞, the patched eigenvariety built from J_B(Π_∞^{R_∞-an}), and the identification of the locally algebraic vectors with π_alg(φ,h) with its multiplicity. The paper is a good source for what those layers have to export downstream — a multiplicity-one statement for Hom(π_alg, Π_∞[a_x]) and the local freeness of the eigenvariety sheaf at a companion point.

AF.5 identifies algebraic modular forms on a group compact at infinity with functions on finite adelic double cosets valued in an algebraic representation. §4.2.2 needs exactly that for a definite unitary group attached to a CM extension, together with its completed p-adic limit Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E); the paper is a good source for the level structures and the coefficient systems (inertial types and lattices W_{ξ,τ}) that the layer must carry.

O0 builds weight spaces and the locally analytic representations that overconvergent families live in. The eigenvariety of §4.2.2 is Emerton's, built from the Jacquet module of a completed Banach space rather than from overconvergent forms, but it lives over the same weight space and its basic geometry (equidimensionality of dimension nd_K, Cohen–Macaulayness of the coherent sheaf, reducedness) is the same package; the paper is a good source for the definite-unitary case of that package.

prerequisites.citation: S. Orlik and M. Strauch, On Jordan–Hölder series of some locally analytic representations, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 28 (2015), 99–157 [55]
prerequisites.why: The single most load-bearing input on the GL_n(K)-side. The functors F^G_{P^-}(M,π) and their Jordan–Hölder theorem give Proposition 3.1 (1) and (4) — the constituents C(w,u) of a locally analytic principal series and when two of them coincide — and are used again in Lemma 3.10 for parabolic inductions. Nothing in the atlas plans them.

prerequisites.citation: S. Orlik, On some properties of the functors F^G_P from Lie algebra to locally analytic representations, arXiv:1802.07514 (2018) [56]
prerequisites.why: Its Theorem 1 gives Proposition 3.1 (2) and (3): the socle of a locally analytic principal series and the socle of its quotient by π_alg, hence the definition of PS_1(w(φ),h) and the identification (3.1) of C(I,s_{i,σ}) as a socle. A load-bearing input that is still a preprint.

prerequisites.citation: M. Emerton, Jacquet modules of locally analytic representations of p-adic reductive groups I, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. 39 (2006), 775–839, and II: The relation to parabolic induction [38], [39]
prerequisites.why: Part I constructs J_B; Part II gives the closed induction I_{P^-}^G, the notion of a balanced map (Def. 0.8) and the adjunction (Thm. 0.13) that converts the tangent-space computation on an eigenvariety into an injection of GL_n(K)-representations. Used at the two decisive steps of §4 (Lemma 4.3 and (4.13)) and throughout §3.1. Part II is cited as ‘to appear’.

prerequisites.citation: P. Schneider and J. Teitelbaum, Algebras of p-adic distributions and admissible representations, Invent. Math. 153 (2003), 145–196 [57]
prerequisites.why: Defines the distribution algebra D(G,E), coadmissible modules and admissible locally analytic representations — the category in which every Ext^1 of the paper is computed. LocallyAnalyticDistributions builds Q_p-analytic distributions on O_F and finite products only, not the algebra of a p-adic reductive group.

prerequisites.citation: B. Schraen, Représentations localement analytiques de GL_3(Q_p), Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. 44 (2011), 43–145 [58]
prerequisites.why: Its Cor. 4.9 is the spectral sequence Ext^p_{T(K)}(H_q(N^-(K),V),δ) ⇒ Ext^{p+q}_G(V,(Ind_{B^-}^G δ)^an) with which Lemma 3.5, Proposition 3.6 and Proposition 3.3 are proved, and its Prop. 4.7 gives the comparison of locally algebraic and locally analytic self-extensions with fixed central character.

prerequisites.citation: J. Bellaïche and G. Chenevier, Families of Galois representations and Selmer groups, Astérisque 324 (2009) [10]
prerequisites.why: §2.3.5 and §2.5.3 construct the trianguline deformation rings and prove the K = Q_p case of Proposition 2.10 (Prop. 2.3.10 and Thm. 2.5.10): the dimension of the trianguline deformation space and the surjectivity of the weight map.

prerequisites.citation: K. Nakamura, Deformations of trianguline B-pairs and Zariski density of two dimensional crystalline representations, J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 20 (2013), 461–568 [51]
prerequisites.why: The general-K replacement for Bellaïche–Chenevier: Cor. 2.53, Prop. 2.41, Lem. 2.56 and Thm. 2.62 give all of Proposition 2.10 and Proposition 2.12, and Thm. 5.11 the comparison of (φ,Γ)-cohomology with the Galois cohomology of a B-pair.

prerequisites.citation: G. Chenevier, On the infinite fern of Galois representations of unitary type, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. 44 (2011), 963–1019 [26]
prerequisites.why: Thm. 3.19 (the surjectivity of the amalgamation of trianguline deformations for K = Q_p) and Prop. 3.6, 3.7 (paraboline deformation spaces), which Proposition 2.13 and Proposition 2.17 generalise to arbitrary K.

prerequisites.citation: R. Liu, Cohomology and duality for (φ,Γ)-modules over the Robba ring, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2007, rnm150 [48]
prerequisites.why: The finiteness and Euler characteristic of (φ,Γ)-cohomology, from which every dimension in §2.3 is computed; with Hom(D,D) = E and Ext^2(D,D) = 0 it gives dim Ext^1(D,D) = 1 + n²d_K.

prerequisites.citation: L. Berger, Construction de (φ,Γ)-modules: représentations p-adiques et B-paires, Algebra Number Theory 2 (2008), 91–120 [7], and Équations différentielles p-adiques et (φ,N)-modules filtrés, Astérisque 319 (2008), 13–38 [6]
prerequisites.why: B-pairs and the functors W_e, W^+_dR (Prop. 2.2.6), used to define D_pst and D_dR of a crystabelline (φ,Γ)-module and, in [6, Thm. A], to identify the filtered module of D_σ with the σ-part of that of D (Proposition 2.5 (2)).

prerequisites.citation: J.-M. Fontaine, Arithmétique des représentations galoisiennes p-adiques, Astérisque 295 (2004), 1–115 [40]
prerequisites.why: Thm. 3.19, the classification of B_dR-representations, is what produces the lattice Λ and hence the modified module D_σ of Proposition 2.5 — the construction on which the whole treatment of a general K rests.

prerequisites.citation: K. Kedlaya, J. Pottharst and L. Xiao, Cohomology of arithmetic families of (φ,Γ)-modules, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 27 (2014), 1043–1115 [44]
prerequisites.why: §6.2 for the rank one modules R_{K,E}(χ), Def. 2.2.2 for the relative Robba ring over an affinoid, and the global triangulation theorem used over the eigenvariety in §4.2.

prerequisites.citation: A. Caraiani, M. Emerton, T. Gee, D. Geraghty, V. Paškūnas and S. W. Shin, Patching and the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, Camb. J. Math. 4 (2016), 197–287 [23]
prerequisites.why: §2 constructs the patched module M_∞ and Π_∞ over R_∞; Thm. 4.35 identifies Π_∞[m_x]^lalg with π_alg(φ,h); Lem. 4.17 and Thm. 4.19 describe the R_∞-action on locally algebraic vectors through the Bernstein centre, and Lem. 3.22 gives the maps J_w used for Proposition 3.3 (2). All of §4.1 rests on it.

prerequisites.citation: C. Breuil, E. Hellmann and B. Schraen, Une interprétation modulaire de la variété trianguline, Math. Ann. 367 (2017), 1587–1645 [21], and Smoothness and classicality on eigenvarieties, Invent. Math. 209 (2017), 197–274 [20]
prerequisites.why: [21] §2.2 constructs the trianguline variety X^□_tri(ρ̄), and its Thm. 1.1, Thm. 2.6 give the embedding of the patched eigenvariety and the smoothness at non-critical points that §4.1 uses verbatim; [20] Lem. 3.8, Lem. 4.16 give the local freeness of the eigenvariety sheaf and the semisimplicity of the Jacquet module at such a point. Note that the authors record in the third paper of the series (extracted as PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19, Remark 1.1 and Prop. 5.4.1) two corrections to these two papers: the hypothesis ᵖ√1 ∉ F is missing from their global results, and the proof of [20, Cor. 5.18] overlooks a Cohen–Macaulayness property.

prerequisites.citation: C. Breuil and F. Herzig, Towards the finite slope part for GL_n, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2020, 10495–10552 [17]
prerequisites.why: Def. 5.7 constructs the amalgamated representation π(ρ)^fs = π(φ,h) whose first two socle layers are π_1(φ,h), and Thm. 5.12 extends an embedding of π_alg(φ,h) into completed cohomology to one of π(φ,h) — used in Remark 4.7 and in the proof of Theorem 4.18.

prerequisites.citation: J. Bergdall, Paraboline variation over p-adic families of (φ,Γ)-modules, Compos. Math. 153 (2017), 132–174 [5]
prerequisites.why: Thm. 5.3 is the global triangulation statement in the paraboline form needed at a smooth point of an eigenvariety: it gives property (iii) of the Galois family in Proposition 4.17 and the trianguline parameter of the deformation attached to a tangent vector in Lemma 4.4.

prerequisites.citation: C. Breuil and Z. Qian, Splitting and expliciting the de Rham complex of the Drinfeld space, arXiv:2407.06651 (2024) [18]
prerequisites.why: Prop. 5.1.14 and Lem. 3.2.4 (ii) give Lemma 3.5 (1), the one-dimensionality of Ext^1_{GL_n}(C(I,s_{i,σ}),π_alg(φ,h)) and of Ext^1_{GL_n}(π_alg(φ,h),C(I,s_{i,σ})). A 2024 preprint carrying a load-bearing step of a published theorem; the paper reproves the second equality by Schraen's spectral sequence and cites Breuil–Ding Cor. 5.9 for the first when K = Q_p.

prerequisites.citation: Y. Ding, Companion points and locally analytic socle for GL_2(L), Israel J. Math. 231 (2019), 47–122 [31], and Simple L-invariants for GL_n, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 372 (2019), 7993–8042 [32]
prerequisites.why: [31, Cor. A.4, Prop. A.5, Lem. 1.15] is the partially de Rham dimension formula on which every statement of §2.3.2 and §2.4 about Ext^1_σ depends; [32, Lem. 2.26] is the push-forward isomorphism for Ext^1 used at least four times in §3.1, and [32, §4.1.2] is the variant of the patched eigenvariety of §4.1.

prerequisites.citation: P. Allen, Deformations of polarized automorphic Galois representations and adjoint Selmer groups, Duke Math. J. 165 (2016), 2407–2460 [1]; J. Newton and J. Thorne, Adjoint Selmer groups of automorphic Galois representations of unitary type, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 25 (2023), 1919–1967 [52]
prerequisites.why: The two sources for Hypothesis 4.15, the vanishing of the adjoint Selmer group, which is the only global input of §4.2 besides classicality; Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen [21, Cor. 4.12] is the third.

prerequisites.citation: T. Barnet-Lamb, T. Gee, D. Geraghty and R. Taylor, Local-global compatibility for l = p, II, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. 47 (2014), 165–179 [2]
prerequisites.why: With Breuil–Ding (6.3) it gives the classicality input (4.14): the locally algebraic vectors of Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E)[m_ρ] are π_alg(φ,h)^{⊕r}. Without it §4.2 has no starting point.

prerequisites.citation: G. Chenevier, Familles p-adiques de formes automorphes pour GL_n, J. Reine Angew. Math. 570 (2004), 143–217 [28]; L. Nyssen, Pseudo-représentations, Math. Ann. 306 (1996), 257–283 [53]
prerequisites.why: Chenevier Prop. 7.1.1 interpolates the pseudo-characters of the classical points over an affinoid of the eigenvariety; Nyssen Thm. 1 identifies deformations of an absolutely irreducible ρ with deformations of its trace, which is what makes T(U^℘)/a_T ≅ R_{ρ,U}/a_ρ in §4.2.2.

prerequisites.citation: J. E. Humphreys, Representations of semisimple Lie algebras in the BGG category O, Amer. Math. Soc. (2008) [43]
prerequisites.why: The standard facts on Verma modules, their composition factors and the dot action that Proposition 3.1 and Lemma 3.10 quote; the Tau Ceti Lie highest weight roadmap plans Verma modules over a field, but not over the product Lie algebra gl_{n,Σ_K}.

sourceIssues.reason: C(I,s_{i,σ}) is defined for I ⊂ {1,…,n} of cardinality i, and π_1(φ,h) is built on p. 35 as an extension of the direct sum of ALL of them — ‘(2^n-2)d_K constituents in total’, i.e. Σ_{i=1}^{n-1} C(n,i) = 2^n-2 summands for each σ. The stated dimension is the one used everywhere afterwards (Remark 3.22 computes dim Ker(t_D) = (2^n - n(n+1)/2 - 1)d_K from it), so it is the index set that is wrong.

Page 38 prints the index set as 'I⊂{1,...,n−1},#I=i' in (3.12) and, in the same proposition, 'dim_E Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h), π_1(φ,h)) = n + (2^n − 1)d_K'. gaps.detail: Hypothesis 4.10 (on a subspace Ext^1_U(D,D) of the local deformation space) and Hypothesis 4.15 (the injectivity of Ext^1_{g,S_p∖{℘}}(ρ,ρ) → Ext^1(D,D)/Ext^1_g(D,D), i.e. the vanishing of the adjoint Selmer group) are hypotheses, and Theorem 4.18 and Corollaries 4.20–4.21 hold under them. A design job must plan them as hypotheses and record where they are known — Allen, Thm. A; Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen [21, Cor. 4.12]; Newton–Thorne, Thm. A — not as targets. The same holds for the standing assumptions of §4.1: that Π_∞[m_x]^lalg ≠ 0 for some maximal ideal of R^℘_∞[1/p], and the Taylor–Wiles hypotheses built into the patched module of [23], which the paper does not restate.

Remark 1.2 (4) states that π_1(D) (= π_min(D)) ‘should still be far from the final complete locally analytic GL_n(K)-representation associated to D’, which is why the notation π(D) is avoided, and Remark 4.7 that π_fs(D) ‘should still be far from the entire Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[m_x]’. These are expectations, not theorems; no layer may take them as statements to prove. Likewise the introduction's remark that for K ≠ Q_p there remain further parameters beyond {D_σ}_{σ∈Σ_K} (references [15, §3] and [34, Conj. 1.7]) is an open direction, not a result of this paper.

Three steps are explicitly left to the reader and must be supplied by a formalisation: Proposition 2.23 (the existence and uniqueness of the modified deformation D̃_σ, ‘the same argument as in the proof of Proposition 2.5, accounting for the E[ϵ]/ϵ²-structure. We leave the details to the reader’); Proposition 2.35 (3) (the σ-analogue of Lemma 2.28, ‘the dévissage arguments in the proof of Lemma 2.28 work when Ext^1's are all replaced by Ext^1_σ's, by [31, Prop. A.5]. We leave the details to the reader’); and Proposition 3.6 (1) (the bijectivity of (3.10), ‘follows from similar arguments as in the proof of Lemma 3.5 … We leave the details to the reader’). The last of these carries the dimension count n + nd_K on which Proposition 3.8 and hence Theorem 3.21 rest.

Several inputs are quoted from sources written for K = Q_p or for a different group, with the assertion that the arguments generalise. Proposition 2.13 cites Chenevier [26, Prop. 3.6, Prop. 3.7] ‘which is for K = Q_p, but all the arguments generalize directly to general K’ (the paper does give the general argument for the partially de Rham analogue in Proposition 2.17). Lemma 2.1 is proved by ‘a straightforward generalization of the proof of [15, Lem. 5.1] to finite extensions K of Q_p’. Lemma 4.4 uses Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen [20, Lem. 4.16] ‘which directly generalizes to the crystabelline case’. Proposition 4.14 (1) (2) ‘follows verbatim’ from four lemmas of [21] and [20] applied to a different Banach representation, and (3) ‘by the same argument as in [29, Prop. 3.9]’. The patched eigenvariety of §4.1 is quoted from Ding [32, §4.1.2], described as ‘an easy variation’ of the patched eigenvariety of [21]. Each of these is a real obligation, not a citation.

Three overloadings will break a formalisation if carried over. (i) h^1 and h^2 have two different meanings inside §3.1.3: first the blocks of h cut out by a P-filtration (p. 40), then (p. 43, as in §2.4) the truncations (h_1,…,h_{n-1}) and (h_2,…,h_n). (ii) The symbol 𝔗_σ denotes both the operation on weights, on modules (D ↦ D_σ), on sets ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) → ΦΓ_nc(φ,𝔗_σ(h)) and on deformation spaces (2.27). (iii) Ext^1_g, Ext^1_{g'}, Ext^1_w and Ext^1_{F_P} are used both for (φ,Γ)-modules and, with the same names, for GL_n(K)-representations; the whole content of Theorem 3.21 is that the two families correspond, so a plan must keep them apart and state the correspondence as a theorem.

Two steps of the published paper depend on work that is not published: Lemma 3.5 (1) — the one-dimensionality of Ext^1 between π_alg(φ,h) and a constituent C(I,s_{i,σ}) — cites Breuil–Qian, arXiv:2407.06651 (2024), Prop. 5.1.14 and Lem. 3.2.4 (ii); and Proposition 3.1 (2) (3) cites Orlik, arXiv:1802.07514 (2018), Thm. 1, for the socle of a locally analytic principal series. Emerton's ‘Jacquet modules II’, whose Thm. 0.13 is used twice in §4, is cited as ‘to appear’. A design job should either route the missing proofs or record the dependence explicitly.
